stem.en: Why did the continuous energy spectrum of beta-decay electrons force Pauli to propose a new, undetected particle?
stem.et: Miks sundis beetalagunemise elektronide pidev energiaspekter Paulit ette panema uut, tuvastamata osakest?

label.en: Because a fixed nuclear mass difference should give a single fixed electron energy, so a continuous spectrum meant a second particle had to be sharing the available energy unevenly.
label.et: Sest fikseeritud tuumamassi vahe peaks andma ühe fikseeritud elektroni energia, seega pidev spekter tähendas, et teine osake pidi saadaolevat energiat ebaühtlaselt jagama.

label.en: Because the electron was already known to be too heavy to have been sitting inside the nucleus beforehand.
label.et: Sest teati juba, et elektron on liiga raske, et olla eelnevalt tuuma sees istunud.

label.en: Because the neutrino had already been directly detected experimentally, and Pauli was just explaining the existing data.
label.et: Sest neutriino oli juba otse eksperimentaalselt tuvastatud, ning Pauli lihtsalt seletas olemasolevaid andmeid.

label.en: Because beta decay was observed to emit no electron at all, only invisible radiation.
label.et: Sest täheldati, et beetalagunemine ei kiirga üldse elektroni, ainult nähtamatut kiirgust.
